why_use_this: Reach for this package whenever you have a scalar or vector field expressed as a vāṇी function pointer -- not sampled data, not a symbolic expression -- and need a differential-calculus quantity (gradient, divergence, curl, Laplacian) or a multi-dimensional/line integral evaluated numerically at a point or over a region. Every differential operator here is a central finite difference (accurate to \( O(h^2) \), tunable via the step size `h` you pass in), and every integral is Simpson's rule applied along each axis via [vani-calculus](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-calculus)'s `integrate_simpson`. This is the numerical, not symbolic, side of vector calculus -- if you want an exact symbolic derivative or antiderivative instead of a numeric approximation at a point, that's [vani-symbolic](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-symbolic)'s job, not this package's.

math_notes.vc_gradient_2d: \( \nabla f = \left( \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}, \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} \right) \), each partial derivative approximated by the central difference \( \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} \approx \dfrac{f(x+h,y) - f(x-h,y)}{2h} \).
math_notes.vc_gradient_3d: \( \nabla f = \left( \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}, \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}, \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial z} \right) \), each component the same central-difference approximation as `vc_gradient_2d`, one dimension deeper.
math_notes.vc_divergence_2d: \( \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = \dfrac{\partial F_x}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial F_y}{\partial y} \) for a vector field \( \mathbf{F} = (F_x, F_y) \), each partial a central difference.
math_notes.vc_divergence_3d: \( \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = \dfrac{\partial F_x}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial F_y}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial F_z}{\partial z} \) for \( \mathbf{F} = (F_x, F_y, F_z) \).
math_notes.vc_curl_2d: The scalar 2D curl \( \dfrac{\partial F_y}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial F_x}{\partial y} \) -- the z-component of the full 3D curl for a field with no z-dependence, which is all a 2D field can meaningfully report (curl is inherently a 3D rotation-axis concept; 2D collapses it to a single signed scalar).

math_notes.vc_laplacian_2d: \( \nabla^2 f = \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \), each second partial via the standard 3-point central difference \( \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \approx \dfrac{f(x+h,y) - 2f(x,y) + f(x-h,y)}{h^2} \).
math_notes.vc_laplacian_3d: \( \nabla^2 f = \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial z^2} \), each term the same 3-point central difference as `vc_laplacian_2d`, one dimension deeper.
math_notes.vc_double_integral: \( \displaystyle\int_{a_y}^{b_y}\!\!\int_{a_x}^{b_x} f(x,y) \; dx\,dy \), computed as nested composite Simpson's rule: sample \( f \) on an \( n \times n \) grid, integrate along \( x \) for each fixed \( y_j \) to get one value per row, then integrate that result along \( y \) -- true nested Simpson's rule via pre-sampling (see the README's "no closures" note for why pre-sampling, not a nested function call, is how this composes).
math_notes.vc_triple_integral: \( \displaystyle\int_{a_z}^{b_z}\!\!\int_{a_y}^{b_y}\!\!\int_{a_x}^{b_x} f(x,y,z)\; dx\,dy\,dz \), the same nested-Simpson's-via-pre-sampling pattern as `vc_double_integral`, one dimension deeper.
math_notes.vc_line_integral_2d: \( \displaystyle\int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \; dt = \int_a^b \big( F_x(\mathbf{r}(t)) \, r_x'(t) + F_y(\mathbf{r}(t)) \, r_y'(t) \big) \, dt \) along a parametrized curve \( \mathbf{r}(t) = (r_x(t), r_y(t)) \) for \( t \in [a,b] \), evaluated via 1D composite Simpson's rule on the dot-product integrand -- the same builtin this package reuses to verify the 2D divergence theorem (`vc_double_integral` of a field's divergence over a square equals the sum of its outward flux across all four edges via this function).
math_notes.vc_line_integral_3d: \( \displaystyle\int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \; dt \) for a 3D parametrized curve \( \mathbf{r}(t) = (r_x(t), r_y(t), r_z(t)) \), the same dot-product-then-1D-Simpson's pattern as `vc_line_integral_2d`, one dimension deeper.
